title: Akamai launches managed inference and isolated agent execution
dek: New managed services pair model serving with runtime containment for autonomous agents at the edge.
evidence: Akamai vendor announcement; no independent latency or security assessment supplied
takeaway: Test sandbox escape resistance, filesystem and network policy, cold starts and observability before adopting an agent runtime.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: A model-serving endpoint and the code executed on an agent's behalf have different isolation and scaling requirements.

paragraphs: An agent needs two runtimes: A model-serving endpoint and the code executed on an agent's behalf have different isolation and scaling requirements.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: A managed service handles model execution, authentication and requests over Akamai Cloud.

Agent code runs using Akamai Functions, while code it creates executes in a separate WebAssembly-isolated environment implemented with the Spin framework; resource and network capabilities can be constrained.

paragraphs: Akamai Inference: A managed service handles model execution, authentication and requests over Akamai Cloud.

Akamai Agent Sandbox: Agent code runs using Akamai Functions, while code it creates executes in a separate WebAssembly-isolated environment implemented with the Spin framework; resource and network capabilities can be constrained.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Akamai describes its architecture but does not publish independent container-escape testing or apples-to-apples p95 latency comparisons against microVMs.
Wasm isolation constrains compute, memory and system capabilities. It does not establish that a permitted outbound request or tool action is safe.

paragraphs: Vendor capability statement: Akamai describes its architecture but does not publish independent container-escape testing or apples-to-apples p95 latency comparisons against microVMs.
Boundary: Wasm isolation constrains compute, memory and system capabilities. It does not establish that a permitted outbound request or tool action is safe.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.lead: Separate host risk from agent policy
bullets.detail: Limit filesystem and egress capabilities, then separately check tool permissions and user authorization for state-changing actions.
Test cold starts, multi-tenant separation, egress rules, long-running tools and p95 round-trip latency against containers or microVMs.
